title: IvyBridge Systems - sovereignty & throughput renewal check-in
summary: Quarterly renewal/expansion check-in focused on EU data residency, throughput SLAs and committing to an uplift. Customer leaning toward dedicated capacity with V P C tunnel, asked for perf benchmarks and encryption/K M S details. Agreed next steps: send updated SOW/pricing, share SOC2+ISO doc bundle, schedule dedicated latency run next week.
action_items: Samir - send updated pricing grid and redline SOW - 2026-05-28
Lena - produce 95/99 latency P50/P95 tails from similar eu-hosted customers (anonymized) - 2026-06-01
Priya - share 3 representative prompt sets and token distribution for bench - 2026-05-28
Marcus - confirm networking constraints (eg egress rules, NAT) and preferred region (eu-west-1) - 2026-05-29
next_steps: Samir to attach security package and SOC2/ISO artifacts to email
Schedule 2-hour dedicated throughput run w/ Redwood SE next Tue 10am UTC

Follow-up call to confirm commitment amendment by 2026-06-04
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-05-26 16:00 UTC | Duration: 48m
Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Lena (Redwood SE), Diego (CSM), Tom (IvyBridge CTO), Priya (Head of ML), Marcus (Infra), Nora (Procurement)

Summary (auto): quick renewal check-in, customer leaning dedicated, heavy EU residency, wants perf bench, security docs, pricing rework.

00:00 Tom: yeah thanks everyone, um we'll keep this tight, Nora is here for procurement questions too
00:12 Samir: great, appreciate it. quick agenda - capacity uplift, private egress/V P C, SLA and security, and next steps
00:27 Priya: to set context - our volume has increased about 3x since Jan, token mix is heavier on generation, P95 latency is creeping and some customers in the EU flagged residency concerns
00:44 Lena: okay, that's helpful. are you seeing bursty tail behavior or more sustained throughput need?
00:51 Priya: mostly steady with spikes around batch jobs, and we need a predictable p95 at 500ms or lower for our chat flows
01:06 Marcus: network-wise we prefer eu-west-1, we can open required ports but will need an explicit V P C peering or private link - we can't expose data to public egress
01:22 Samir: good, Dedicated + VPC is definitely a scenario we've done. question on commitment: are you looking at a 12 month extension with an uplift or a pilot-first approach?
01:36 Tom: prefer pilot->commit. procurement wants to see SLA math and encryption at rest keys - K M S integration with our HSM is necessary for compliance.
01:50 Diego: noted, we have K M S integration patterns and H S M connectors — we'll pull the docs. Do you need on-prem packaging or will a customer-managed key in the cloud suffice?
02:06 Tom: cloud K M S with customer-managed keys is fine as long as we get audit logging per token or request level (or close).
02:18 Priya: also we want to run a performance replay with our prompt sets to validate P95 at target and to check cost per token impact when moving to quantized variants
02:33 Lena: perfect — for the bench we usually run a 2 hour sustained run plus burst windows to simulate spikes. we'll need your token distribution and sample prompts.
02:45 Priya: will share the three sets after this call
02:52 Samir: on pricing — two levers: reserved Dedicated buckets (committed monthly) or pay-as-you-go hosted with reserved burst. Dedicated gives lower unit cost and predictable tails but requires a commit.
03:10 Marcus: if committed, what's the fallback if usage drops? can we reduce capacity mid-contract?
03:18 Samir: we can include a staged ramp clause; typical is quarter-by-quarter amendments with a 20% downsize window at each renewal with pro rata adjustments
03:30 Nora: procurement - we'll need payment terms and an updated SOW to show to legal; also curious if you support net-60 on enterprise deals
03:44 Samir: we can discuss net-60 for enterprise, will confirm with finance. SOW will include activation timeline, region, and failover playbook.
03:57 Tom: security - SOC2 plus ISO artifacts? and can you provide encryption key rotation policy?
04:06 Diego: yes SOC2 and ISO bundle available, key rotation is customer-controlled with options for rotation cadence, we log rotation events in audit trail
04:18 Priya: about model selection — we tested a smaller q4 quantized variant to cut cost but saw hallucination increase; can Redwood recommend model/quantization profiles by workload?
04:33 Lena: absolutely, Redwood Optimize does that; SEs will recommend a profile — we'll include quality regression checks in the bench so we can compare outputs objectively
04:48 Tom: competitors - we've had outreach from GiantCloud AI and FathomServe pitching lower latency in eu-central. why choose Redwood?
04:58 Samir: a few reasons — consistent cross-environment API (hosted/dedicated/private), the cost controls (batching/caching), and ops tooling: per-route tracing and token-level cost breakdown. also our fallbacks for capacity are baked into routing policies
05:15 Marcus: latency guarantees? we need P95 SLA language for dedicated in the SOW
05:22 Samir: we can propose a P95 SLA target and a credits-based remedy for breaches; we'll show historical p95 numbers from similar customers (anonymized)
05:32 Priya: good. for the bench, can we enable prefix caching? some of our flows are repetitive so cache would reduce cost and improve latency if compatible
05:44 Lena: yes, we can enable prefix/K V cache for the bench and measure hit rates; note caching semantics differ by request shape, we'll capture that metric
05:58 Tom: timeline — procurement wants a decision in two weeks to align with budget cycles
06:04 Samir: that timeline works if we turn around pricing and security bundle within 48 hours and run the bench early next week
06:12 Nora: legal will want indemnity language and data residency clauses, what region residency guarantees do you offer for EU customers?
06:22 Diego: we support region pinning and option for Private (customer-controlled control plane) for strict data residency; we'll include data flow diagrams for legal
06:36 Priya: quick nit — sometimes in transcripts I see you write 'Redwood dedicate' which confused internal teams; just call it Redwood Dedicated in docs please
06:46 Samir: noted, we'll standardize nomenclature.
06:52 Tom: anything else?
07:00 Samir: recap of commitments: we will send SOW/pricing and security bundle; Lena will run bench plan, customer shares prompts; schedule bench Tue 10am UTC. Next call to review bench results and SOW.
07:18 Priya: thanks all
07:21 Tom: thanks
07:24 (call ends)

Notes: transcript has occasional mis-hearings (e.g., K M S rendered as KMS/K M S inconsistently), speaker overlaps minimal.
